messages:
marta: Heads-up — cluster telemetry for the last 14 days shows a weird pattern: small long-tail tenants are causing persistent fragmentation in several pools, and we're seeing a set of 'underserved buckets' that never get a contiguous slot allocation. Can we quickly sync on whether to run a conservative compaction + reweighting before Q3 surge planning? :thinking_face:

ajay: Can you paste the top-line numbers? is this concentrated in a region/pool?

marta: Summary: eu-west and us-central pools show ~6.8% fragmentation (unused GPU fraction due to slot gaps). That maps to ~2.4k GPU-hours/week wasted across the fleet. Most of it is small 0.25-2 GPU requests that never consolidate. Also, reserved dedicated pools with mixed tenant mixes are worse.

noah: Oof. Those small fractional requests are the classic long-tail. Did the sim run on the new slot-fit heuristics?

marta: I re-ran the quick sim with the slot-fit bump + soft eviction budgets. Results:
- compact-on-drain + delayed prewarm reduces fragmentation to ~2.1%
- estimated savings ~1.7k GPU-hours/week (so net waste down to ~700 GPU-hours/week)
- tail latency impact for 95th percentile of small jobs is +6-9ms in canary, within SLOs

sasha: Where did you bias the fairness weight? iirc we tried tilt toward 1-GPU tenants last quarter and it skewed long-run fairness.

marta: I used a transient bias: tenant_weight *= 0.85 for >8h inactive windows, and a small favor to consolidate nodes (node_consolidation_score += 0.15). It's a short-run policy for compaction windows only. Not a permanent weight change.

ajay: Do we have costs translated? 1.7k GPU-hours/week saved -> what's $/week?

marta: Back-of-envelope: average spot-equivalent $0.7/hr -> ~$1.2k/week saved. Over a month that's ~5k. Also reduces cross-AZ network egress in some reshuffles.

noah: I'm worried about multi-tenant fairness regressions. Can we limit compaction to tenants below X concurrent GPUs or opt-in?

marta: Plan:
1) run targeted compaction in eu-west and us-central on weekend window (Sat 02:00-06:00 local) for a week as a canary
2) compaction only for tenants with <=2 concurrent GPUs and <3 active jobs in last 15m
3) apply soft eviction budgets (max preempt per-node=1) and prefer node-local migration where possible
4) measure: fragmentation, 95/99 p99 small-job latency, tenant fairness delta (alloc rate over last-30d)

sasha: Add a kill-switch to abort if tenant fairness delta > 3% or if any tenant reports >2x job failures in canary window.

marta: Good call. Will do. Also pushing a slight tweak to the scheduler config for the canary:

```\n# canary compaction config
compaction:
  enabled: true
  target_tenants: "<=2gpus && <3jobs_15m"
  max_preempt_per_node: 1
  consolidation_score_bias: 0.15
  transient_tenant_weight_multiplier: 0.85
```\n
ajay: Who's owning the rollout? I can take the canary run and dashboards.

marta: Thanks — plz own run + dashboards, @ajay. I'll handle the scheduler config push and the compaction job. @noah can you run the fairness regression check and set up alerts?

noah: Yep. I'll wire a short eval that compares per-tenant allocation rate pre/post and alert on >2.5% delta.

infra-bot: scheduled compaction canary created by marta for clusters [eu-west, us-central] at 2026-03-21T02:00Z — job id: compaction-1763214321-01

ajay: Dashboards I'll add: fragmentation heatmap, wasted GPU-hours estimate, per-tenant allocation rate, small-job tail latency. Will post links before rollout. :thumbsup:

marta: Timeline: roll canary this weekend (Sat), collect 48h of metrics, decide Mon EOD. If green -> expand to apac-lite pool next weekend. If negative -> abort and revert scheduler config.

sasha: If canary is green, can we fold the transient policy into the weekly maintenance job instead of always-on? That reduces risk.

marta: Yes — that's the plan. Weekly maintenance compaction window with the transient bias. Only if metrics stay good we consider more frequent runs.

noah: Quick ask: can we cap compaction moves per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors (max_moves_per_tenant=2)?

marta: Done. I'll include that in the job.

ajay: Cool. I'll post the dashboard links and the run notes here once ready.

sasha: Thanks team — nice surgical approach.

marta: Thanks — will update thread with results. :rocket:
